TEMPO: Temporary or temporarily. A NOTAM and meteorological qualifier indicating that a condition, restriction, or weather phenomenon is expected to last for a limited duration only.
TF: Track to fix. A leg type in area navigation (RNAV) defined by a track between two waypoints without a specified altitude or speed constraint.
TFC: Traffic. A general aviation term referring to aircraft, vehicles, or personnel operating on an aerodrome or within controlled airspace; used in ATC communications to indicate other aircraft in the vicinity.
TGL: Touch-and-go landing. A flight manoeuvre in which an aircraft lands on a runway and immediately takes off again without coming to a full stop, commonly used for pilot training.
TGS: Taxiing guidance system. A ground-based system providing directional guidance to pilots during taxi operations, often using visual indicators or surface lighting to aid navigation on the aerodrome manoeuvring area.
THR: Threshold. The beginning of that portion of a runway usable for landing; marked by specific runway markings and lighting, and may be displaced for obstacle clearance or noise abatement.
THRU: Through. Used in NOTAM text and flight planning to indicate a range or span of values, times, or positions, e.g., 'Monday THRU Friday'.
THU: Thursday. A day-of-week abbreviation used in NOTAM text and aviation scheduling to specify the day an event or operation occurs.
TIL: Until. A temporal qualifier in NOTAM text and flight documentation indicating the end time or date of a validity period.
TKOF: Take-off. The phase of flight during which an aircraft accelerates along the runway and becomes airborne; used in NOTAMs for runway closures, obstructions, or restrictions affecting departure operations.
TLOF: Touchdown and lift-off area. A load-bearing area on a helideck or heliport designated for the touchdown and lift-off of helicopters, typically marked and lit for safe day and night operations.
TMA: Terminal control area. A controlled airspace established at the confluence of ATS routes in the vicinity of one or more major aerodromes, designed to manage arriving and departing IFR traffic.
TNA: Turn altitude. The altitude at which an aircraft is required to commence a turn during an instrument approach or departure procedure, ensuring obstacle clearance and procedure compliance.
TNH: Turn height. The height above a specified reference datum (typically aerodrome elevation) at which an aircraft must begin a turn during an instrument procedure.
To (followed by place). Used in NOTAM text and flight planning to indicate a destination or direction, e.g., 'TO KLAX'.
TOC: Top of climb. The point in a flight profile at which an aircraft reaches its initial cruising altitude after departure, marking the transition from climb to cruise phase.
TODA: Take-off distance available. The length of the take-off run available plus the length of any clearway beyond the runway end, representing the total distance available for an aircraft to accelerate, lift off, and climb to a specified height.
TORA: Take-off run available. The length of runway declared available and suitable for the ground run of an aircraft during take-off, as published in aerodrome documentation.
TOX: Toxic. A hazard classification used in NOTAM text and cargo documentation to indicate the presence of poisonous or harmful substances that may affect ground handling or emergency response.
TP: Turning point. A defined geographical location at which an aircraft changes heading during a flight, used in air navigation procedures, military operations, and VFR waypoint navigation.
TR: Track. The actual path of an aircraft over the ground, expressed as a compass direction; distinct from heading, as it accounts for wind drift effects.
TRA: Temporary reserved airspace. Airspace of defined dimensions designated for temporary exclusive or restricted use by specific activities, such as military exercises or special operations, and activated via NOTAM.
TRANS: Transmits or transmitter. Used in NOTAM text and ATC communications to refer to a radio transmission or the equipment that sends radio frequency signals.
TREND: Trend forecast. A landing forecast appended to a METAR report, providing expected changes in weather conditions (wind, visibility, cloud) for the next two hours at the aerodrome.
TRG: Training. An abbreviation used in NOTAMs and flight scheduling to indicate areas, times, or activities dedicated to flight instruction, simulator training, or military readiness exercises.
TRL: Transition level. The lowest flight level above the transition altitude at which aircraft flying in the standard pressure setting (1013.25 hPa) operate, ensuring vertical separation consistency between altimeter settings.
TROP: Tropopause. The boundary layer between the troposphere and the stratosphere, characterised by a temperature inversion; its altitude is used in aviation weather analysis and flight level planning.
TT: Teletypewriter. A legacy electromechanical communications device historically used for transmitting NOTAM and AFTN messages over dedicated telegraph circuits.
TUE: Tuesday. A day-of-week abbreviation used in NOTAM text and aviation scheduling to specify the day an event or operation occurs.
TURB: Turbulence. Irregular and unpredictable movement of air causing aircraft to experience sudden changes in altitude or attitude; reported in PIREPs and forecasts as light, moderate, severe, or extreme.
TVOR: Terminal VOR. A very high frequency omnidirectional range station installed at or near an aerodrome to provide terminal-area navigation guidance for approaching and departing aircraft.
TWY: Taxiway. A defined path on an aerodrome designated for the taxiing of aircraft connecting runways with aprons, hangars, and other facilities.
TXL: Taxilane. A portion of an apron or ramp area designated as a taxi route for aircraft moving to or from a parking position, typically not part of the formal taxiway system.
TYP: Type of aircraft. A code or description identifying the specific make and model of an aircraft, used in flight plans, NOTAMs, and traffic management for separation and performance assessment.
TYPH: Typhoon. A severe tropical cyclone occurring in the Northwest Pacific region, producing extreme winds, heavy rain, and turbulence that significantly impact flight operations.
U/S: Unserviceable. A status indicator in NOTAM text denoting that a facility, system, or component is not operational or is unavailable for its intended use.
UA: Unmanned aircraft. An aircraft operated without a pilot on board, commonly referred to as a drone; used in NOTAMs to designate UAS operating areas and restrictions.
UAB: Until advised by. A temporal qualifier in NOTAM text indicating that a condition or restriction remains in effect until further notification from the issuing authority.
UAC: Upper area control centre. An ATC facility responsible for providing air traffic control services to IFR flights in upper airspace above a specified altitude, typically above FL 245.
UAR: Upper air route. An ATS route established in upper airspace, typically above a specified transition altitude, used for en-route IFR navigation.
UAS: Unmanned aircraft system. The complete system comprising an unmanned aircraft, its remote pilot station, control link, and any other associated components; used in NOTAMs and regulations governing drone operations.
UFN: Until further notice. A NOTAM time qualifier indicating that a condition, restriction, or activation is in effect indefinitely until officially cancelled or updated.
UHDT: Unable higher due traffic. A pilot or ATC communication stating that a requested higher altitude cannot be assigned because of conflicting traffic in the airspace above.
UIC: Upper information centre. An ATS unit providing flight information and alerting services to aircraft operating in upper airspace, primarily in regions without full radar coverage.
ULR: Ultra long range. A classification for aircraft capable of flying non-stop distances exceeding approximately 8,000 nautical miles, enabling intercontinental operations without refuelling.
UNA: Unable. A phrase used in ATC and NOTAM text to indicate that a requested action, clearance, or service cannot be accommodated.
UNAP: Unable to approve. A NOTAM or ATC response indicating that a requested operation, flight plan, or activity cannot be authorised due to operational constraints.
UNL: Unlimited. Used in NOTAM text and meteorological reports to indicate no upper limit, such as unlimited ceiling (sky condition) or unrestricted visibility.
UNREL: Unreliable. A status qualifier in NOTAMs and technical documentation indicating that a navigational aid, communication system, or reported data cannot be trusted for operational use.
UTA: Upper control area. A controlled airspace above a specified altitude, typically extending from the upper limit of a terminal control area up to the lower limit of the upper flight information region.
